note: Verified statute sections per state and question. Each was found by an agent reading the downloaded open-us-law text and is kept only if the reference resolves and the quote appears in the section.

records.act: Alaska Public Records Act (AS 40.25.100-40.25.295)
records.quote: the public records of all public agencies are open to inspection by the public under reasonable rules during regular office hours. The public officer having the custody of public records shall give on request
alternates: 40.25.123 (Department of Administration adopts regulations implementing AS 40.25.110-40.25.140)
40.25.120 (exceptions; not present in the downloaded file)
records.why: AS 40.25.110 is the core inspection-on-request section of the Act: it opens records to inspection, requires the custodian to supply copies when asked, and sets the fees, including the five-person-hour rule. The statute sets no response deadline. Under AS 40.25.123, the request-and-response timelines are left to regulations (2 AAC 96), which are not in this file. AS 40.25.120 (exceptions) is missing from the downloaded statutes.

business.act: Alaska Revised Limited Liability Company Act (AS 10.50)
business.quote: One or more persons may organize a limited liability company by signing articles of organization and delivering the signed articles to the department for filing.
business.why: AS 10.50.070 is the section that forms an LLC by signing articles of organization and delivering them for filing. Section 10.50.075 covers only what the articles must contain, 10.50.080 sets when the company is organized, and 10.50.850 sets the fees.

records.act: Alabama Open Records Act (Ala. Code §§ 36-12-40 et seq.)
records.quote: (3) The public officer shall acknowledge a proper request within 10 business days of receiving the request.
alternates: 36-12-40 (right to inspect and copy public writings; exceptions)
36-12-41 (copies on request and payment of fees)
36-12-45 (written procedures; request form; how to submit a request)
records.why: § 36-12-44 sets the core response procedure: request form/procedures, fees, acknowledgment within 10 business days, substantive response within 15 business days (45 for time-intensive), and presumed denial. § 36-12-45 covers how a resident submits a request and is the closest alternate. The earlier guess § 22-36-4 was a keyword hit outside the act.

business.act: Alabama Limited Liability Company Law of 2014 (Ala. Code Title 10A, Chapter 5A)
business.quote: In order to form a limited liability company, one or more organizers must execute a certificate of formation and deliver it for filing to the filing officer provided for in subsection (e).
alternates: 10A-5A-2.02 (amendment or restatement of certificate of formation)
business.why: This section forms an LLC by filing a certificate of formation with the Secretary of State. It also lists what the certificate must contain and says when the company is formed.

records.act: Arizona Public Records Law (A.R.S. Title 39, Chapter 1, Article 2)
records.quote: Any person may request to examine or be furnished copies, printouts or photographs of any public record during regular office hours
alternates: A.R.S. § 39-121.02 (action on denial of access; costs, fees, damages)
A.R.S. § 39-121.03 (requests for commercial purpose; statement of purpose)
39-121.01(E): access deemed denied if custodian fails to promptly respond
records.why: 39-121.01(D) sets out how any person requests to examine or receive copies (in person or by mail), requires the custodian to promptly furnish them and provide an index of withheld records, and (E) treats a failure to respond promptly as a denial. That is the core request-and-response procedure. 39-121 only states the general right of inspection.

business.act: Arizona Limited Liability Company Act (A.R.S. Title 29, Chapter 7)
business.quote: One or more persons may act as organizers to form a limited liability company by delivering to the commission for filing the articles of organization.
alternates: A.R.S. § 29-3203 (signing of records delivered for filing)
A.R.S. § 29-3202 (amendment or restatement of articles of organization)
business.why: 29-3201 is titled 'Formation of limited liability company; articles of organization'. It covers forming an LLC by delivering articles to the Corporation Commission, lists what the articles must contain (subsection B), and says the LLC is formed once the articles take effect (subsection D).

records.act: California Public Records Act (Gov. Code § 7920.000 et seq.)
records.quote: Each agency, upon a request for a copy of records, shall, within 10 days from receipt of the request, determine whether the request, in whole or in part, seeks copies of disclosable public records
alternates: 7922.530 (Cal. Gov. Code § 7922.530: records promptly available upon request reasonably describing identifiable records, upon payment of duplication fees)
records.why: CPRA as recodified in 2023; 7922.535 sets the 10-day determination and notice duty and the extension rules, which is the core response procedure. 7922.530 (copy request and fees) is the companion request section. Both bare refs printed the GOV sections.

business.act: California Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act (Corp. Code § 17701.01 et seq.)
business.quote: One or more persons may act as organizers to form a limited liability company by signing and delivering to the Secretary of State for filing articles of organization on a form prescribed by the Secretary of State.
alternates: 17702.01(b) required contents of the articles of organization (same section)
17702.01(d) LLC formed when the Secretary of State files the articles (same section)
business.why: 17702.01 covers formation by filing articles of organization, their contents, and when the LLC is formed (subdivision (d)). The bare ref printed Cal. CORP § 17702.01. I did not find or print a fee section.

records.act: Connecticut Freedom of Information Act
records.quote: (b) Nothing in the Freedom of Information Act shall be construed to require disclosure of:
alternates: 1-206 (denial of access; appeals to FOI Commission; the four-business-day deemed-denial rule is in its subsection (a))
records.why: Sec. 1-210 'Access to public records. Exempt records.' is the CT FOIA's core access section: its subsection (a) gives every person the right to inspect records promptly during regular office hours and to get copies. In this downloaded file, though, the printed text begins at subsection (b), the exemptions. Subsection (a) of 1-206 (the four-business-day response rule) also fails to print, and the text search for 'promptly during regular office hours' / 'four business days' found nothing. So the quote can only come from the printed (b) text. The section is the right one, but the file's text is incomplete.

business.act: Connecticut Uniform Limited Liability Company Act
business.quote: (d) A limited liability company is formed on the date and at the time of its filing by the Secretary of the State, as provided in section 34-247e .
alternates: 34-247a (amendment or restatement of certificate of organization)
business.why: The heading 'Formation of limited liability company. Certificate of organization.' matches, and the text sets out the required contents of the certificate and says the LLC is formed when the Secretary of the State files it. Subsection (a) (the form-by-delivering-certificate language) is missing from the file's printed text, but (b)-(d) confirm this is the right section. No LLC-specific fee section was found under chapter 613a (34-250 is not in the file).

records.act: Delaware Freedom of Information Act
records.quote: The public body shall respond to a FOIA request as soon as possible, but in any event within 15 business days after the receipt thereof
records.why: Section 10003 covers how to make a request: it must be in writing, it must describe the records, and each body has a FOIA coordinator. Subsection (h) sets the 15-business-day deadline to respond. The bare number 10003 is used in several titles, so the ref has to include the title.

business.act: Delaware Limited Liability Company Act
business.quote: In order to form a limited liability company, 1 or more authorized persons must execute a certificate of formation. The certificate of formation shall be filed in the office of the Secretary of State
alternates: 6 Del. C. § 18-202 (amendment to certificate of formation)
business.why: Section 18-201 forms the LLC: the certificate of formation is filed with the Secretary of State and lists its required contents. Subsection (b) says the LLC exists once the certificate is filed. The bare ref 18-201 prints the right section.

records.act: Florida Public Records Act (Chapter 119, Florida Statutes)
records.quote: A custodian of public records and his or her designee must acknowledge requests to inspect or copy records promptly and respond to such requests in good faith.
records.why: Section 119.07 sets the core inspection-and-copying duty. It requires custodians to acknowledge requests promptly, respond in good faith, and state the basis for any exemption. It also covers fees.

business.act: Florida Revised Limited Liability Company Act (Chapter 605, Florida Statutes)
business.quote: One or more persons may act as authorized representatives to form a limited liability company by signing and delivering articles of organization to the department for filing.
business.why: Section 605.0201 is the formation section: an LLC is formed by delivering articles of organization for filing. The same section lists what the articles must contain, and subsection (4) says when the company is formed.

records.act: Uniform Information Practices Act (Modified), HRS ch. 92F
records.quote: each agency shall make available for public inspection and duplication during regular business hours:
alternates: 92F-11 (General rule; request-and-response provision; NOT in downloaded file)
92F-23 (individual's access to own personal record; 10 working days, extendable 20)
records.why: The core section for requesting records is HRS § 92F-11 (open to inspection; each agency must make records available upon request). That section is missing from the downloaded HI statutes: `lexflow statute hi "92F-11"` returns not found, and a text search for "92F-11" finds no copy of it. Other ch. 92F sections are present (92F-2, -3, -12, -13, -14, -15, -15.5, -16, -19, -22, -23, -27, -42). The fallback ref given here is 92F-12 (Disclosure required), the closest section that is present: it lists the records each agency must make available. It does not set out the request-and-response procedure. Response deadlines for UIPA requests are in OIP rules, not in the statute. The earlier guess, 523A-20, is wrong. It is in the unclaimed property chapter, not UIPA.

business.act: Hawaii Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, HRS ch. 428
business.quote: One or more persons may organize a limited liability company, consisting of one or more members, by delivering articles of organization to the office of the director for filing.
business.why: § 428-202 (Organization) is the formation section. An LLC is organized by delivering articles of organization for filing, and (b) says it exists once the articles are filed. § 428-203 covers what the articles must contain. § 428-206 covers how the director files them. I did not find the fee section.

records.act: Iowa Open Records Law (Iowa Code ch. 22, Examination of Public Records)
records.quote: In writing, by telephone, or by electronic means. The lawful custodian of the records shall post information for making such requests in a manner reasonably calculated to apprise the public of that information.
alternates: Iowa Code § 22.3 (supervision and fees; custodian must fulfill written, phone, or electronic requests and tell the requester about expenses when the request arrives)
Iowa Code § 22.2 (right to examine and copy; exceptions)
Iowa Code § 22.8 (injunction; subsection 4 allows good-faith delay, normally no more than 10 business days and never more than 20 calendar days)
records.why: Section 22.4, titled 'Public records requests', is the section that says how a person makes a request: in person during office hours, or in writing, by phone or electronically. Chapter 22 has no single request-and-response section. Section 22.3 covers how the custodian fulfills requests and charges fees, and the only response deadline is in § 22.8(4)(d), which limits delay to 20 calendar days. Section 22.8 is mainly the injunction section, so the earlier guess was wrong. Section 22.2 is the right-to-examine section.

business.act: Iowa Uniform Limited Liability Company Act (Iowa Code ch. 489)
business.quote: One or more persons may act as organizers to form a limited liability company by delivering to the secretary of state for filing a certificate of organization.
alternates: Iowa Code § 489.202 (amendment or restatement of certificate of organization)
business.why: Section 489.201 forms the LLC when a certificate of organization is filed with the secretary of state. It also sets the required contents and says the company is formed when the certificate becomes effective.

records.act: Idaho Public Records Act
records.quote: A public agency or custodian shall either grant or deny a resident's request to examine or copy public records within three (3) working days of the date of the receipt of the request for examination or copying.
alternates: 74-102 (right to examine; written request contents; fees)
records.why: 74-103, titled 'Request and response to request for examination of public records', says requests go to the designated custodian. It sets the grant-or-deny deadlines: 3 working days for residents and 21 days for nonresidents, extendable to 10 working days or 35 days. It also covers deemed denial and the written denial notice. 74-102 covers the right to examine, what a request must contain, and fees, so it is listed as an alternate.

business.act: Idaho Uniform Limited Liability Company Act
business.quote: One (1) or more persons may act as organizers to form a limited liability company by delivering to the secretary of state for filing a certificate of organization.
business.why: 30-25-201 is the formation section. Organizers deliver a certificate of organization to the secretary of state, and subsection (d) says the LLC is formed when the certificate becomes effective. The same section lists what the certificate must contain. The filing fees are in 30-21-214, which was found by heading search but not printed.

records.act: Illinois Freedom of Information Act
records.quote: Each public body shall, promptly, either comply with or deny a request for public records within 5 business days after its receipt of the request, unless the time for response is properly extended under subsection (e) of this Section
records.why: 5 ILCS 140/3 is the FOIA's core request-and-response section (records available for inspection, how to make a request, 5-business-day deadline to comply or deny, extensions). It is in the file: a statute-search --text for '^\(5 ILCS 140/3\)' matches one section, 'Section 3' (1111 words), and the quoted sentence is an exact regex match in that same section. I could not print it with the statute tool, though. The ref '5 ILCS 140/3 § 3' (also '5 ILCS 140 § 3') prints 225 ILCS 140/3, the Volunteer Health Practitioners act, instead. The cause is find() in lexflow/municipal/statutes.py: it matches the article name as a case-insensitive substring of the citation and returns the first hit, and '5 ILCS 140/3' is a substring of '225 ILCS 140/3'. No article string can pick out 5 ILCS 140 until the lookup is anchored, for example by requiring a word boundary or start-of-string before the article. The bare '3' fails as ambiguous. Confidence is medium only because the tool cannot print this section.

business.act: Illinois Limited Liability Company Act
business.quote: One or more persons, other than natural persons under 18 years of age, may organize a limited liability company by executing and delivering articles of organization to the Secretary of State as specified in Sections 5-5 and 5-45.
alternates: 805 ILCS 180/5-5 § 5-5 (contents of articles of organization; (b) company is organized when articles are filed by the Secretary of State)
805 ILCS 180/50-10 § 50-10 (fees; $150 for filing articles of organization)
business.why: Printed 805 ILCS 180/5-1 (Organization). It is the formation section: a company is organized by executing and delivering articles of organization to the Secretary of State. Section 5-5 (contents, plus when organization takes effect), 5-45 (execution and filing) and 50-10 (fees) were all printed and are listed as alternates. Refs of the form '805 ILCS 180/N § N' print correctly.

records.act: Indiana Access to Public Records Act (IC 5-14-3)
records.quote: If the public agency does not deny the request, within a reasonable time after the request is received by the agency the public agency shall either:
alternates: Ind. Code § 5-14-3-9 (denial of disclosure, response deadlines, action to compel)
records.why: Section 3 sets out the right to inspect and copy, what a request must contain (reasonable particularity, writing at the agency's discretion), and the agency's duty to respond within a reasonable time. Section 9 holds the denial procedure and timing for denials.

business.act: Indiana Business Flexibility Act (IC 23-18)
business.quote: At least one (1) person may form a limited liability company by causing articles of organization to be executed and filed for record with the office of the secretary of state.
alternates: Ind. Code § 23-0.5-9-19 (filing fee for articles of organization: $75 electronic, $100 otherwise)
Ind. Code § 23-18-1-3 (definition of articles of organization)
business.why: This section is the formation-by-filing provision, and it also lists what the articles must contain. The filing fee is in the Uniform Business Organizations Code at IC 23-0.5-9-19.

records.act: Kansas Open Records Act
records.quote: Each request for access to a public record shall be acted upon as soon as possible, but not later than the end of the third business day following the date that the request is received.
alternates: 45-220 (agency procedures for requesting access to and obtaining copies of records)
records.why: 45-218 is the KORA inspection, request and response section. It covers the right to inspect, requests made to someone other than the custodian, the three-business-day deadline to act on a request, a written statement of the grounds for a denial, and fees.

business.act: Kansas Revised Limited Liability Company Act
business.quote: In order to form a limited liability company, one or more authorized persons must execute articles of organization. The articles of organization shall be filed with the secretary of state and set forth:
alternates: 17-7911 (effective date of filed documents; formation time)
17-76,136 (fees for documents filed with the secretary of state)
business.why: 17-7673 is the section that forms an LLC by executing articles of organization and filing them with the secretary of state. It also lists what the articles must contain, and subsection (b) points to 17-7911 for when the company is formed.

records.act: Kentucky Open Records Act (KRS 61.870 to 61.884)
records.quote: The official custodian may require a written application, signed by the applicant and with his or her name printed legibly on the application, describing the records to be inspected.
alternates: KRS § 61.880 (agency must decide within five days, excluding weekends and holidays, and notify the requester in writing; Attorney General review)
records.why: 61.872 sets out the request procedure: who may inspect, the written application, how it can be delivered (hand, mail, fax, e-mail), and the custodian's duties, including the five-day limit when records are unavailable. The general five-day response deadline is in 61.880(1), so it is listed as an alternate.

business.act: Kentucky Limited Liability Company Act (KRS Chapter 275)
business.quote: One (1) or more persons may serve as the organizer and form a limited liability company by delivering articles of organization to the Secretary of State for filing.
business.why: 275.020 is titled 'Procedure for forming limited liability company'. It forms the LLC by delivering articles of organization to the Secretary of State for filing, and existence begins when they are filed. The fee section (KRS 14A.2-060) is not in the downloaded file.

records.act: Louisiana Public Records Law (La. R.S. 44:1 et seq.)
records.quote: If the public record applied for is immediately available, because of its not being in active use at the time of the application, the public record shall be immediately presented to the authorized person applying for it.
alternates: La. R.S. 44:32 (ref "La. Rev. Stat. § 44: § 32"): duty to present records on request, copies and fees, and a 5-day written notice when the custodian questions whether something is a public record
La. R.S. 44:31 (ref "La. Rev. Stat. § 44: § 31"): right to examine records
records.why: 44:33 (Availability of records) is the request-and-response rule. It covers what happens 'when a request is made for a public record': the record is shown right away, or if it is in active use the custodian must certify that in writing and set a time within three business days. 44:32 sets the custodian's duty to present records and copies and the 5-day notice when access is questioned, so it is the main alternate. Bare numbers are ambiguous in this file and the citation is stored as 'La. Rev. Stat. § 44:33', so the working ref needs the title prefix before ' § 33'. I tested the ref and it prints the right section.

business.act: Louisiana Limited Liability Company Law (La. R.S. 12:1301 et seq.)
business.quote: One or more persons capable of contracting may form a limited liability company by filing the articles of organization and the initial report with the secretary of state.
alternates: La. R.S. 12:1305 (ref "La. Rev. Stat. § 12: § 1305"): contents of the articles of organization and the initial report
La. R.S. 12:1309: amendment of articles of organization
La. R.S. 49:222: fees chargeable by the secretary of state (found by heading search, not printed)
business.why: 12:1304 (Formation) forms an LLC by filing the articles of organization and initial report with the secretary of state, who then issues a certificate of organization. 12:1305 covers contents only. I tested the ref with the statute tool and it prints the right section.

records.act: Massachusetts Public Records Law (G.L. c. 66, §§ 10-10A; definition in G.L. c. 4, § 7, cl. 26)
records.quote: shall at reasonable times and without unreasonable delay permit inspection or furnish a copy of any public record as defined in clause twenty-sixth of section 7 of chapter 4
alternates: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66 § 10A (appeal to supervisor of records; superior court review)
Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66 § 6A (records access officers)
Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 4 § 7 cl. 26 (definition of public records and exemptions)
Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66 § 10(d) (fees, inside the same section)
records.why: I printed ch. 66 § 10, headed 'Inspection and copies of public records; requests; written responses; extension of time; fees'. It is the core request-and-response section. It says how a request is delivered (by hand, first class mail or email to the records access officer), sets the 10-business-day deadline to respond, lists what a written response must contain, and sets the 15/25-day production limits and the extension petitions. The bare number '10' is ambiguous in the MA file, so the ref includes the chapter. The old guess 'not found' was wrong.

business.act: Massachusetts Limited Liability Company Act (G.L. c. 156C)
business.quote: In order to form a limited liability company, one or more authorized persons must execute a certificate of organization. The certificate of organization shall be filed in the office of the state secretary
alternates: Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 156C § 12(d) (filing fee of $500, inside the same section)
Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 156C § 13 (amendment of certificate of organization)
Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 156C § 14 (cancellation of certificate of organization)
Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 156C § 5 (office and resident agent required in the certificate)
business.why: I printed ch. 156C § 12, headed 'Certificate of organization'. It is both the formation-by-filing section and the contents section, and subsection (b) says the LLC is formed when the certificate is filed with the state secretary. The filing fee is in § 12(d) of the same section. The old guess 'ch. 223 sec 12' named the wrong chapter. Bare '12' is ambiguous, and the ref 'Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 156C § 12' prints the right section.

records.act: Maine Freedom of Access Act (1 M.R.S. §§ 400-414)
records.quote: shall acknowledge receipt of a request made according to this section within 5 working days of receiving the request and may request clarification concerning which public record or public records are being requested.
alternates: 1 M.R.S. § 400 (short title: Freedom of Access Act)
1 M.R.S. § 408-A(8)-(11) (fees, estimates, waivers, within same section)
records.why: Section 408-A sets out the right to inspect and copy public records and how a request works: it need not be in person or in writing, receipt is acknowledged within 5 working days, a good-faith estimate of time and cost follows, and written notice of any denial is due within 5 working days. Section 400 confirms the subchapter is the Freedom of Access Act. The bare ref 408-A printed the right section.

business.act: Maine Limited Liability Company Act (31 M.R.S. ch. 21)
business.quote: A limited liability company is formed at the time of the filing of the initial certificate of formation in the office of the Secretary of State
alternates: 31 M.R.S. § 1532 (amendment or restatement of certificate of formation)
31 M.R.S. § 1673 (requirements for documents filed with the Secretary of State)
5 M.R.S. § 105(1) (registered agent information required in the certificate)
business.why: Section 1531 requires that a certificate of formation be signed and filed with the Secretary of State, lists what it must contain, and says the LLC is formed when it is filed. The bare number 1531 is ambiguous (it also exists in Titles 5, 10 and 22), so the title-qualified ref '31 M.R.S. § 1531' is needed. That ref printed the right section.

records.act: Michigan Freedom of Information Act
records.quote: a public body shall, subject to subsection (10), respond to a request for a public record within 5 business days after the public body receives the request by doing 1 of the following
records.why: MCL 15.235 (FOIA sec. 5) covers the written request to the FOIA coordinator and the 5-business-day response options (grant, deny, partial, or a 10-day extension). It is the core request-and-response section.

business.act: Michigan Limited Liability Company Act
business.quote: One or more persons, who may or may not become members, may be the organizers of a limited liability company by filing executed articles of organization.
business.why: MCL 450.4202 forms the LLC when executed articles of organization are filed. Existence begins on the articles' effective date.

records.act: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act (Minn. Stat. ch. 13)
records.quote: Upon request to a responsible authority or designee, a person shall be permitted to inspect and copy public government data at reasonable times and places
alternates: Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(c) (copies and fees; copies supplied as soon as reasonably possible)
Minn. Stat. § 13.03, subd. 3(f) (denial must cite the statute)
Minn. Stat. § 13.04 (rights of data subjects; 10-business-day response)
records.why: Section 13.03, Access to Government Data, is the core public-access procedure. Subd. 2 makes entities set up procedures so requests are handled promptly. Subd. 3 covers the right to inspect and copy, fees, the timing of copies, and denial notices that must cite the statute. I printed and checked it.

business.act: Minnesota Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act (Minn. Stat. ch. 322C)
business.quote: One or more persons may act as organizers to form a limited liability company by signing and filing with the secretary of state articles of organization.
alternates: Minn. Stat. § 322C.0201, subd. 2 (required contents of articles)
Minn. Stat. § 322C.0201, subd. 4 (formed on filing with $135 payment)
business.why: Section 322C.0201 is titled Formation of Limited Liability Company; Articles of Organization. Organizers form the company by filing articles with the secretary of state. Subd. 2 lists the required contents, and subd. 4 says the company is formed on filing with the $135 fee. I printed and checked it.

records.act: Missouri Sunshine Law (Mo. Rev. Stat. ch. 610)
records.quote: Each request for access to a public record shall be acted upon as soon as possible, but in no event later than the end of the third business day following the date the request is received
records.why: 610.023 requires a custodian, makes records available for inspection and copying, sets the three-business-day response deadline, and covers written grounds for denial. It is the Sunshine Law's core request-and-response section.

business.act: Missouri Limited Liability Company Act (Mo. Rev. Stat. ch. 347)
business.quote: Any person, whether or not a member or manager, may form a limited liability company by signing and filing articles of organization for such limited liability company with the secretary.
business.why: 347.037 is the section that forms an LLC: the company comes into existence when the articles of organization are filed with the secretary of state. 347.039 only lists what the articles must contain, and 347.179 sets the fees.

records.act: Montana Public Records Act (Title 2, ch. 6, part 10)
records.quote: A person may request public information from a public agency. A public agency shall make the means of requesting public information accessible to all persons.
alternates: 2-6-1009 (written notice of denial -- failure to meet response deadline -- civil action)
records.why: 2-6-1006 is the core request-and-response procedure. It covers how a person requests public information and how local governments must respond (in a timely manner). Other agencies must acknowledge receipt within 5 business days and provide a single, readily available record within 5 working days, or else give a time and fee estimate. Fees are also covered.

business.act: Montana Limited Liability Company Act (Title 35, ch. 8)
business.quote: One or more persons may form a limited liability company consisting of one or more members by signing and filing articles of organization with the secretary of state.
business.why: 35-8-201 'Formation' is the section that forms an LLC by filing articles of organization, and it says existence begins on filing. The contents section (35-8-202) is not in the downloaded file: the statute tool returned 'not found'. No separate LLC fee section was found in the 35-8 headings.

records.act: North Carolina Public Records Act (G.S. Chapter 132)
records.quote: Every custodian of public records shall permit any record in the custodian's custody to be inspected and examined at reasonable times and under reasonable supervision by any person
alternates: 132-6.2 (Provisions for copies of public records; fees)
records.why: 132-6 is the core inspection/copy request provision: custodians must permit inspection by any person and furnish copies as promptly as possible; requester need not state purpose. NC has no fixed day-count deadline other than 'as promptly as possible'.

business.act: North Carolina Limited Liability Company Act (G.S. Chapter 57D)
business.quote: One or more persons may cause an LLC to be formed by delivering executed articles of organization to the Secretary of State for filing in accordance with this Chapter and Chapter 55D of the General Statutes.
business.why: 57D-2-20 is titled 'Formation' and provides that an LLC is formed by delivering articles of organization to the Secretary of State for filing, effective when filed.

business.act: North Dakota Uniform Limited Liability Company Act (N.D. Cent. Code ch. 10-32.1)
business.quote: One or more individuals of the age of eighteen years or more or other persons may act as organizers to form a limited liability company by signing and filing with the secretary of state articles of organization
alternates: 10-32.1-21 (amendment or restatement of articles of organization)
10-32.1-86 (filing of records with secretary of state - effective date)
10-32.1-92 (fees; cited by 10-32.1-20 but not in the downloaded file)
business.why: This section forms an LLC by filing articles of organization with the secretary of state. In the same section, subsection 2 lists the required contents and subsection 4 says the LLC is formed on filing. The fee section 10-32.1-92 is missing from the downloaded statutes.

records.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 84-712 (not in downloaded file)
records.act: Nebraska Public Records Statutes
records.why: The request-and-response section of Nebraska's public records law is Neb. Rev. Stat. 84-712, and the related sections run from 84-712 through 84-712.09. None of these are in the downloaded ne file. The statute tool returns 'section ... not found' for 84-712, 84-712.01, 84-712.04 and 84-712.05. A heading search for '84-' finds only 64 sections in Chapter 84, from 84-101 to 84-219, so the file stops before the 84-7xx sections. A text search for '84-712' only turns up sections in other chapters that cite it.

business.act: Nebraska Uniform Limited Liability Company Act
business.quote: One or more persons may act as organizers to form a limited liability company by signing and delivering to the Secretary of State for filing a certificate of organization
alternates: 21-118 (amendment or restatement of certificate of organization)
21-192 (filing fees, including $110/$100 for certificate of organization under 21-117)
business.why: This section (RULLCA 201) covers forming the company by filing a certificate of organization with the Secretary of State. It lists what the certificate must contain and says the company is formed once the Secretary of State files it. Section 21-118 covers amendments only, and 21-192 sets the fees.

records.act: New Hampshire Right-to-Know Law (RSA ch. 91-A, Access to Governmental Records and Meetings)
records.quote: If a public body or agency is unable to make a governmental record available for immediate inspection and copying the public body or agency shall, within 5 business days of a request:
alternates: N.H. Rev. Stat. § 91-A:7-b (complaint process with the ombudsman)
N.H. Rev. Stat. § 91-A:7 (violation/petition to superior court)
records.why: RSA 91-A:4 IV sets out the core procedure: records reasonably described are made available when immediately available, otherwise within 5 business days the agency must produce, deny, or give a written time estimate, and a denial must cite the exemption. Every section in this file has section_number set to the part after the colon, so a bare '4' is ambiguous (it also matches 491-A:4). The ref '§ 91-A:4 § 4' uses the citation substring '§ 91-A:4' to pick it out, and the tool prints the right section with it.

business.act: New Hampshire Revised Limited Liability Company Act (RSA ch. 304-C)
business.quote: In order to form a domestic limited liability company, one or more authorized persons shall deliver a certificate of formation to the secretary of state for filing.
alternates: N.H. Rev. Stat. § 304-C:30 (filing and certification of certificates)
N.H. Rev. Stat. § 304-C:28 (requirements for filing documents)
N.H. Rev. Stat. § 304-C:29 (effective time and date)
N.H. Rev. Stat. § 304-C:34 (amendments to certificates of formation)
business.why: RSA 304-C:31 is the formation section. It requires a certificate of formation to be delivered to the secretary of state, lists what the certificate must contain, and says the LLC is formed when the certificate is filed. The ref is written as '§ 304-C:31 § 31' because bare section numbers repeat across chapters. The tool prints the correct section with this ref.

records.act: New Jersey Open Public Records Act (OPRA), P.L.1963, c.73 (C.47:1A-1 et seq.)
records.quote: The custodian of a government record shall permit the record to be inspected, examined, and copied by any person during regular business hours
alternates: N.J.S.A. 47:1A-6 (proceeding to challenge denial of access)
records.why: 47:1A-5 is OPRA's core access/request section: custodian must permit inspection and copying, sets copy fees and special service charges, and requires a response 'as soon as possible, but not later than seven business days after receiving the request' (14 for commercial purposes). Bare '1A-5' is ambiguous across NJ titles and 'N.J. Stat. § 47:1A-5' fails because the stored section number is '1A-5'; the ref 'N.J. Stat. § 47 § 1A-5' prints the right section. The prior guess 2A:44-45 was wrong.

business.act: New Jersey Revised Uniform Limited Liability Company Act, P.L.2012, c.50 (C.42:2C-1 et seq.)
business.quote: One or more persons may act as organizers to form a limited liability company by signing and delivering to the filing office for filing a certificate of formation.
alternates: N.J.S.A. 42:2C-19 (amendment or restatement of certificate of formation)
N.J.S.A. 42:2C-9 (use of name other than actual LLC name)
business.why: 42:2C-18 forms an LLC by filing a certificate of formation and lists the required contents. Subsection d says the company is formed when the filing office files the certificate and the company has at least one member. Bare '2C-18' is ambiguous because 45:2C-18 also exists, so the ref names title 42. A heading search of chapter 2C found no separate filing-fee section.

records.act: New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act
records.quote: A custodian receiving a written request shall permit the inspection immediately or as soon as is practicable under the circumstances, but not later than fifteen days after receiving a written request.
records.why: 14-2-8 'Procedure for requesting records' sets out how to submit an oral or written request, required contents, and the 3-business-day / 15-day response deadlines.

business.act: New Mexico Limited Liability Company Act
business.quote: One or more persons may form a limited liability company by filing articles of organization with the commission [secretary of state].
alternates: 53-19-10 (effect of filing of articles of organization)
business.why: 53-19-7 'Formation' is the section authorizing formation of an LLC by filing articles of organization; 53-19-10 states when formation is effective.

records.act: Nevada Public Records Act (NRS Chapter 239)
records.quote: Not later than the end of the fifth business day after the date on which the person who has legal custody or control of a public book or record of a governmental entity receives a written or oral request
alternates: 239.010 (public books and records open to inspection)
records.why: 239.0107 is the core request-and-response section. It sets the 5-business-day deadline and lists what the entity must do: grant access, refer the requester to the custodian, give notice of delay, or deny in writing with a citation.

business.act: Nevada Limited-Liability Companies (NRS Chapter 86)
business.quote: One or more persons may form a limited-liability company by signing and filing with the Secretary of State articles of organization for the company.
alternates: 86.161 (articles of organization: required and optional provisions)
business.why: 86.151 is the LLC formation-by-filing section. The prior guess, 692B.160, is wrong: it is not in the LLC chapter.

records.act: New York Freedom of Information Law (Public Officers Law Article 6)
records.quote: Each entity subject to the provisions of this article, within five business days of the receipt of a written request for a record reasonably described, shall make such record available to the person
alternates: N.Y. PBO Law § 87 (access to agency records; rules, fees, exemptions in 87(2))
N.Y. PBO Law § 89(4) (appeals and Article 78 review, within § 89)
records.why: POL § 89(3)(a) sets the written-request procedure and the five-business-day response/acknowledgment deadline; § 89(4) has the appeal. § 87 covers agency rules, fees and exemptions. The earlier guess, PBO Law § 95, belongs to the Personal Privacy Protection Law (Article 6-A), which is a different statute.

business.act: New York Limited Liability Company Law
business.quote: One or more persons may act as an organizer or organizers to form a limited liability company by (i) preparing the articles of organization of such limited liability company
alternates: N.Y. LLC Law § 203(e) (contents of articles of organization, within § 203)
N.Y. LLC Law § 209 (filing with department of state)
business.why: LLC Law § 203 is titled Formation. It says an LLC is formed by preparing, signing and filing articles of organization, and that it exists from the moment of filing. The earlier guess, MHY Law § 31.22, is a Mental Hygiene Law provision about approving certificates. I did not print the alternates for §§ 206, 209 and 1101, so they come from knowledge of the statute rather than from this file.

records.act: Ohio Public Records Act
records.quote: Upon request by any person and subject to division (B)(8) of this section, all public records responsive to the request shall be promptly prepared and made available for inspection to the requester at all reasonable times during regular business hours.
alternates: Ohio Rev. Code § 149.43(A) (definitions and exclusions, same section)
Ohio Rev. Code § 149.43(C) (mandamus enforcement, same section)
Ohio Rev. Code § 149.011 (definitions of public office/records)
records.why: Ohio's Public Records Act request-and-response procedure is in division (B) of § 149.43 (prompt preparation, copies at cost within a reasonable time). Definitions and enforcement are in the same section; the alternates were not printed separately.

business.act: Ohio Revised Limited Liability Company Act (Chapter 1706)
business.quote: In order to form a limited liability company, one or more persons shall execute articles of organization and deliver the articles to the secretary of state for filing.
alternates: Ohio Rev. Code § 111.16 (secretary of state filing fees)
business.why: § 1706.16 forms the LLC by filing articles of organization with the secretary of state and lists what the articles must contain; the LLC exists once the filing is made. The alternates were not printed for verification.

records.act: Oklahoma Open Records Act
records.quote: A public body must provide prompt, reasonable access to its records but may establish reasonable procedures which protect the integrity and organization of its records
records.why: Section 24A.5 opens records to any person for inspection and copying, and sets the request procedure: request forms, reasonable specificity, fees, and the duty to give prompt, reasonable access with delays limited to preparation time. The bare ref 51-24A.5 only prints a stub listing two versions, so the ref used is the current version, v2 (SB 535, Laws 2025, c. 404). The earlier guess, tit. 12 § 1509, was wrong.

business.act: Oklahoma Limited Liability Company Act
business.quote: One or more persons may form a limited liability company upon the filing of executed articles of organization with the Office of the Secretary of State.
business.why: Section 2004, titled 'Filing the articles of organization', is the section that forms the LLC: the company exists once the articles are filed with the Secretary of State, and filing is conclusive evidence of formation.

records.act: Oregon Public Records Law (ORS 192.311 to 192.478)
records.quote: the public body shall within five business days after receiving the request acknowledge receipt of the request or complete the public body's response to the request
alternates: 192.329 (Public body's response to public records request; complete response within 10 business days after acknowledgment deadline)
records.why: 192.324 sets out how a person makes a written request, the 5-business-day acknowledgment duty, form of copies, fees and the required written request procedure; 192.329 complements it with the completion deadline and contents of the response.

business.act: Oregon Limited Liability Company Act (ORS chapter 63)
business.quote: One or more individuals 18 years of age or older or other entities may form a limited liability company by executing and delivering articles of organization to the office for filing.
alternates: 63.051 (Organization - existence begins when articles filed by Secretary of State)
business.why: 63.044 is the formation section authorizing formation by filing articles of organization; 63.047 lists contents and 63.051 sets when existence begins. No LLC-specific filing fee section was found in chapter 63 (Oregon business filing fees are set in ORS 56.140 / by Secretary of State rule, not verified here).

records.act: Pennsylvania Right-to-Know Law (Act of Feb. 14, 2008, P.L.6, No.3)
records.quote: each record of a county office shall be open for inspection subject to the rules and regulations provided under the act of February 14, 2008 (P.L.6, No.3), known as the Right-to-Know Law.
alternates: 42 Pa.C.S. § 67A03 (requests for law enforcement audio/video recordings, references RTKL open-records officer)
records.why: The Right-to-Know Law is codified in unconsolidated Purdon's (65 P.S. §§ 67.101-67.3104), and the state's file only contains consolidated Pa.C.S. titles. Searches of headings and text for request/response procedure (written request, open-records officer, five business days) found only cross-references: 16 Pa.C.S. § 12306 (quoted, it points to the RTKL) and 42 Pa.C.S. § 67A03 (special law-enforcement recordings procedure). The earlier guess 20 Pa.C.S. § 2210 is wrong. The core request/response sections (65 P.S. §§ 67.703, 67.901) are not in the file.

business.act: Pennsylvania Uniform Limited Liability Company Act of 2016 (15 Pa.C.S. Ch. 88)
business.quote: One or more associations or individuals 18 years of age or older may act as organizers to form a limited liability company by delivering to the department for filing a certificate of organization.
alternates: 15 Pa.C.S. § 8822 (amendment or restatement of certificate of organization)
business.why: Section 8821 is titled 'Formation of limited liability company and certificate of organization.' It sets out formation by filing, the required contents in (b), and when formation takes effect in (f). A bare '8821' is ambiguous (53 Pa.C.S. has the same number), so the ref needs the title prefix.

records.act: Ley de Transparencia y Procedimiento Expedito para el Acceso a la Información Pública (Ley 141-2019)
records.quote: los Oficiales de Información de una entidad gubernamental deberán producir cualquier información pública para su inspección, reproducción o ambos, a petición de cualquier solicitante, a la mayor brevedad posible y dicho término nunca excederá de veinte (20) días laborables
alternates: Ley Transp. P.R. § 6 (Art. 6, Solicitudes: how to make a written or electronic request; Information Officer must acknowledge receipt)
Ley Transp. P.R. § 8 (Art. 8, Cobro de cargos: fees)
Ley Transp. P.R. § 9 (Art. 9, Recurso Especial de Revisión Judicial: appeal to the Court of First Instance)
Ley Transp. P.R. § 5 (Art. 5, Oficiales de Información)
records.why: Art. 7 of Ley 141-2019 sets the response procedure: 20 working days (30 for large or old files), a single 20-day extension, a written denial with legal grounds, the ways to deliver the records, and that no answer counts as a denial. Art. 6 covers how to file the request and is listed as the main alternate. A bare '7' is ambiguous in PR. 'Ley Transp. P.R. § 7' prints the right section.

business.act: Ley General de Corporaciones de Puerto Rico (Ley 164-2009), Capítulo XIX Compañías de Responsabilidad Limitada
business.why: The PR file does not seem to include the General Corporations Act or its LLC chapter. Text searches for 'certificado de formación', 'Departamento de Estado un certificado', 'Ley General de Corporaciones' and 'certificado de incorporación' found nothing from that act. Searches for 'compañía(s) de responsabilidad limitada' found only tax and incentive code sections (e.g., 1020.01, 2054.04). The 19.xx headings belong to other acts (insurance code, vehicle law, etc.), not the LLC chapter.

records.act: Rhode Island Access to Public Records Act
records.quote: A public body receiving a request shall permit the inspection or copying within ten (10) business days after receiving a request.
alternates: 38-2-7 (denial of access; written denial within 10 business days; failure to respond deemed denial)
records.why: 38-2-3 sets the right to inspect/copy, requires written procedures for how to make a request, and sets the 10-business-day response deadline plus a 20-business-day extension, so it is the core request-and-response section. The denial procedure is in 38-2-7 and fees are in 38-2-4.

business.act: Rhode Island Limited Liability Company Act
business.quote: One or more persons may form a limited liability company by delivering or causing to be delivered executed articles of organization for filing with the secretary of state.
alternates: 7-16-65 (filing fees; $150 for original articles of organization)
business.why: 7-16-5, titled Formation, says an LLC is formed by filing articles of organization and is formed once the secretary of state accepts them and issues the certificate. The earlier guess, 7-16-44 (a revocation appeal), was wrong.

records.act: South Carolina Freedom of Information Act
records.quote: Each public body, upon written request for records made under this chapter, shall within ten days (excepting Saturdays, Sundays, and legal public holidays) of the receipt of the request, notify the person making the request of its determination
records.why: Section 30-4-30 gives the right to inspect or copy records and sets fees. Subsection (C) says the public body must give its determination within 10 business days (20 if the record is over 24 months old). It must then produce the records within 30 or 35 calendar days, and a request with no timely response counts as approved. This is the core request-and-response procedure.

business.act: South Carolina Uniform Limited Liability Company Act of 1996
business.quote: One or more persons may organize a limited liability company, consisting of one or more members, by delivering articles of organization to the office of the Secretary of State for filing.
alternates: 33-44-206 (filing in Office of Secretary of State)
business.why: Section 33-44-202 is the formation section: an LLC is organized by delivering articles of organization to the Secretary of State, and it exists once they are filed. Section 33-44-203 covers what the articles must contain, and 33-44-206 covers the filing mechanics.

records.act: South Dakota Public Records Law (SDCL ch. 1-27)
records.quote: The public record officer shall promptly respond to the written request but in no event later than ten business days from receipt of the request.
alternates: 1-27-1 (public records open to inspection and copying)
1-27-38 (civil action or administrative review of denial)
records.why: 1-27-37 sets the written-request procedure: request to the public record officer, response within ten business days by providing, denying, or estimating time, written reasons for denial, and deemed denial if no response. 1-27-1 gives the general right to inspect and copy.

business.act: South Dakota Uniform Limited Liability Company Act (SDCL ch. 47-34A)
business.quote: One or more persons may organize a limited liability company, consisting of one or more members, by delivering articles of organization to the Office of the Secretary of State for filing.
alternates: 47-34A-206 (filing in Office of Secretary of State; effective time)
business.why: 202.1 is the formation section: organizers deliver articles to the Secretary of State, existence begins on filing, and the SOS issues a certificate of organization. 47-34A-202 does not exist in the file. In the downloaded copy of 203, the opening (a) lead-in is missing and the text starts at the contents list.

records.act: Texas Public Information Act (Gov't Code ch. 552)
records.quote: An officer for public information of a governmental body shall promptly produce public information for inspection, duplication, or both on application by any person to the officer.
alternates: Tex. Gov't Code § 552.301 (request for attorney general decision, 10 business days)
records.why: 552.221 is the core request-and-production section: it requires prompt production on application by any person, and if records cannot be produced within 10 business days the officer must certify that in writing and set a date. Printed and checked with both the bare ref and the code-qualified ref.

business.act: Texas Business Organizations Code
business.quote: to form a filing entity, a certificate of formation complying with Sections 3.003, 3.004, and 3.005 must be filed in accordance with Chapter 4.
alternates: Tex. Business Organizations Code § 3.005 (general contents of certificate)
Tex. Business Organizations Code § 3.010 (supplemental LLC certificate contents)
Tex. Business Organizations Code § 4.154 (LLC filing fees, same as 4.152)
Tex. Business Organizations Code § 4.151 (filing fees, all entities)
business.why: Texas LLCs are filing entities under the BOC. 3.001 is the formation section: an entity is formed by filing a certificate of formation, and it exists once that filing takes effect. 3.010 covers what an LLC's certificate must contain, and 4.154 sets the LLC fees. The bare number 3.001 is ambiguous, so the code-qualified ref is needed.

records.act: Utah Government Records Access and Management Act (GRAMA)
records.quote: A person making a request for a record shall submit to the governmental entity that retains the record a written request containing:
alternates: 63G-2-201 (provisions relating to records / right of access)
63G-2-403 (Appeals to the director of the Government Records Office)
records.why: Heading is 'Record request -- Response -- Time for responding'; it sets the written-request requirements and the 10-business-day (5 for expedited) response deadline with approve/deny/notify options.

business.act: Utah Uniform Limited Liability Company Act
business.quote: One or more persons may act as organizers to form a limited liability company by delivering to the division for filing a certificate of organization.
alternates: 48-3a-202 (Amendment or restatement of certificate of organization)
48-3a-203 (Signing of records to be delivered for filing)
48-3a-1103 (Additional requirements for certificate of organization - professional services companies)
business.why: Heading 'Formation of limited liability company -- Certificate of organization'; it covers both the filing that forms the LLC and the required contents (subsection 2), and says when the company is formed.

records.act: Vermont Public Records Act (1 V.S.A. ch. 5, subch. 3)
records.quote: Upon request, the custodian of a public record shall promptly produce the record for inspection or a copy of the record, except that:
alternates: 1 V.S.A. § 316 (access to public records; copying costs)
records.why: Section 318 'Procedure' sets the request-and-response process: 'promptly' means within three business days, written certifications for denials/nonexistent records, up to ten-business-day extension for unusual circumstances, and appeal to the agency head within five business days. Bare '318' is ambiguous across titles, so the ref names 1 V.S.A.

business.act: Vermont Uniform Limited Liability Company Act (11 V.S.A. ch. 25)
business.quote: One or more persons may organize a limited liability company, consisting of one or more members, by delivering articles of organization to the Office of the Secretary of State for filing.
alternates: 11 V.S.A. § 4026 (filing in Office of Secretary of State)
business.why: Section 4022 'Organization' is the formation section. It says an LLC is organized by delivering articles of organization to the Secretary of State, and that its existence begins when they are filed. Section 4023 only lists what the articles must contain. The ref needs the 11 V.S.A. prefix because 4022 and 4023 also appear in other titles.

records.act: Washington Public Records Act (chapter 42.56 RCW)
records.quote: Within five business days of receiving a public record request, an agency, the office of the secretary of the senate, or the office of the chief clerk of the house of representatives must respond in one of the ways provided in this subsection (1)
alternates: RCW 42.56.080 (identifiable records, facilities for copying, availability of public records)
RCW 42.56.100 (protection of public records, public access)
records.why: RCW 42.56.520 'Prompt responses required' sets the core response procedure: respond within five business days by providing the records, giving a link, acknowledging the request with a time estimate, asking for clarification, or denying it, and it also covers written denials and review. RCW 42.56.080 covers how requests are made and is listed as an alternate. Bare section numbers don't work as refs here; the code-qualified form 'RCW 42.56 § 520' printed the section.

business.act: Washington Limited Liability Company Act (chapter 25.15 RCW)
business.quote: In order to form a limited liability company, one or more persons must execute a certificate of formation. The certificate of formation must be delivered to the office of the secretary of state for filing
alternates: Chapter 23.95 RCW Article 2 (filing procedures and fees, cross-referenced)
business.why: RCW 25.15.071 'Formation—Certificate of formation' is both the formation section and the contents section. It requires a certificate of formation to be filed with the secretary of state, lists what it must contain, and says the LLC is formed when the certificate is filed. Fees are handled through chapter 23.95 RCW, which was not looked up here. The ref has to be code-qualified ('RCW 25.15 § 071').

records.act: Wisconsin Public Records Law (Wis. Stat. §§ 19.31-19.39)
records.quote: Each authority, upon request for any record, shall, as soon as practicable and without delay, either fill the request or notify the requester of the authority’s determination to deny the request in whole or in part and the reasons therefor.
records.why: 19.35 'Access to records; fees' holds the right to inspect, how a request is made (sub. (1)(h): request must reasonably describe the record and may be oral) and the response duty and timing (sub. (4)(a): fill or deny as soon as practicable and without delay, with reasons). I printed it and confirmed this.

business.act: Wisconsin Uniform Limited Liability Company Law (Wis. Stat. ch. 183)
business.quote: One or more persons may act as organizers to form a limited liability company by signing and delivering to the department for filing articles of organization.
alternates: 183.0202 (amendment or restatement of articles of organization)
business.why: 183.0201 'Formation of limited liability company; articles of organization' forms an LLC when its articles of organization are filed. It also lists what the articles must contain and says formation happens when they take effect. I printed it and confirmed this.

records.act: West Virginia Freedom of Information Act
records.quote: The custodian, upon demand for records made under this statute, shall as soon as is practicable but within a maximum of five days not including Saturdays, Sundays or legal holidays
alternates: W. Va. Code § 29B-1-3a (notice of requests to registry)
records.why: 29B-1-3 sets the right to inspect, says requests go to the custodian with reasonable specificity, and requires a response within five business days (furnish, schedule inspection, or deny in writing). The dataset stores section_number as the short number ('3') under citation 'W. Va. Code § 29B-1-3', so bare '29B-1-3' fails; the working ref is 'W. Va. Code § 29B-1-§ 3' (article substring '... 29B-1-', number '3').

business.act: West Virginia Uniform Limited Liability Company Act
business.quote: One or more persons may organize a limited liability company, consisting of one or more members, by delivering articles of organization to the office of the Secretary of State for filing
alternates: W. Va. Code § 31B-2-203 (articles of organization contents)
W. Va. Code § 31B-2-204 (amendment or restatement of articles)
business.why: 31B-2-202 'Organization.' is the formation section: you form the company by filing articles with the Secretary of State, and it exists once they are filed. 31B-2-203 only lists what the articles must contain. Ref format is the same workaround as for records: 'W. Va. Code § 31B-2-§ 203' printed the contents section.

records.act: Wyoming Public Records Act
records.quote: All public records shall be released not later than thirty (30) calendar days from the date of acknowledged receipt of the request unless good cause exists preventing release
records.why: 16-4-202 sets out the right of inspection, that applications go to the designated public records person, the 7-business-day notice, immediate release of readily available records and the 30-day release deadline.

business.act: Wyoming Limited Liability Company Act
business.quote: One (1) or more persons may act as organizers to form a limited liability company by signing and delivering to the secretary of state for filing articles of organization.
alternates: 17-29-202 (amendment or restatement of articles of organization)
17-29-205 (delivery to and filing of records by secretary of state; effective time and date)
business.why: 17-29-201 is the section on forming an LLC: it covers filing articles of organization, what they must contain, and when the company is formed. A separate fee section did not turn up among the sections checked.
